papers.title: Executive and language systems competitively shape predictive processing during reading
papers.reason: Human TMS, n-back, reading, and computational decision modelling directly examine how working memory and executive control shape predictive processing under cognitive load.

papers.title: Reward changes the use and structure of predictive spatial maps
papers.reason: The paper presents a biologically grounded reinforcement-learning model of reward-dependent spatial representations, relevant to planning and navigation but less directly focused on human executive function.

papers.title: Intrinsic network dynamics catalyze switching in functional connectivity states of the brain
papers.reason: Human fMRI findings link dynamic network switching to cognitive state transitions and working-memory performance, offering useful constraints for models of cognitive control.

papers.title: Acoustic and Attentional Challenges Shape the Balance Between Attended and Competing Speech Tracking Differently
papers.reason: Across multiple human EEG datasets, the study characterizes selective auditory attention and cortical tracking under acoustic and attentional challenge, directly informing models of attention.

papers.title: Medicating inhibitory control? Treatment with serotonergic antidepressants predicts stop-N200 amplitudes in major depressive disorder
papers.reason: This directly examines EEG ERP correlates of inhibitory control in major depressive disorder using stop-N200 amplitudes, making it highly relevant to neural modelling of executive control.

papers.title: Altered emotional inhibitory control in adolescents with high social anxiety: electrophysiological evidence from ERP and connectivity
papers.reason: This is centrally about electrophysiological and connectivity markers of emotional inhibitory control in a human clinical-risk adolescent group.

papers.title: Role of Sports in Holistic Psychosocial Interventions for Substance Use Disorders
papers.reason: The paper mainly reviews sports-based psychosocial interventions for substance use disorders and only tangentially discusses prefrontal executive functions and self-regulation.

papers.title: Pregnancy History and Loss of Normal PSEN2 Function Impact Female Late-Life Cognitive Processing, Inhibitory Signaling, and Gliosis
papers.reason: The title suggests relevance to late-life cognitive processing and inhibitory neural signaling, but the connection to executive function modelling or assessment is indirect from the available information.

papers.title: Neural Bases for Working Memory of Natural Sound Textures
papers.reason: This human fMRI and behavioural study directly investigates auditory working-memory maintenance and neural representations in auditory cortex and medial temporal lobe.

papers.title: The Role of Childhood Traumatic Experiences in Cognitive Flexibility During Early Adulthood
papers.reason: This human behavioural study focuses on cognitive flexibility, an executive function, but relies on questionnaire measures and is only moderately informative for computational modelling or assessment.

papers.title: Anatomical Connectivity of the Macaque Gaze-following Patch
papers.reason: This macaque tracer study maps connectivity of a gaze-following attention region and could inform models of social attention, though it is not directly about executive control or cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Developmental disruption of the mediodorsal thalamus alters prefrontal dopamine D2 receptor expression and prefrontal–accumbal neuronal recruitment during latent inhibition
papers.reason: This rat study links mediodorsal thalamus disruption to selective attention deficits and prefrontal dopamine circuit recruitment, providing mechanistic findings relevant to models of cognitive control.
